newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expected to sign pipeline regulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to sign pipeline regulation bill.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was expected to sign legislation this weekend to give oil and natural gas pipeline operators more leeway in meeting safety regulations, congressional aides said on Friday.
Under the bill, regulators will have to take more account of cost-benefit studies and risk analyses before imposing new rules. Critics have dubbed it the "pipeline deregulation" bill.
"We were told by the White House that President Clinton will sign the bill on Saturday," said an aide to New Jersey Democratic Rep. Frank Pallone, who opposed the measure.
The Transportation Department's Office of Pipeline Safety and the Energy Department endorsed the bill, which also has the backing of the pipeline industry.

Supporters of the bill said it would let regulators and pipeline companies focus on pipelines that pose the greatest risk to public safety, and give pipeline companies more freedom to develop plans to improve safety.

"I am concerned that the White House, as well as many of the congressmen and senators who supported the bill, may not have had all the information they needed to make the right decision," Pallone said in a statement.

Under the new law, there would be fewer required pipeline inspections, laxer safety requirements for pipeline operators and weaker environmental protection, said Pallone, who had a major pipeline explosion in his district in 1994.

Julie Stewart, spokeswoman for the American Gas Association, said: "This is not a deregulation bill. It does not get rid of previous regulations, but it does give pipeline operators the flexibility to do what's best for their own individual systems."
The Senate passed the bill unanimously, while the House passed it 276-125.
